clips.title: 🔥 The Ultimate Guide to Disaster Recovery: RTO, RPO, & Failover!
clips.why: Two words from disaster recovery give names to this lesson's question: how much work may we lose (RPO), and how fast must we be back (RTO).
look: RPO is measured back from the failure to the last save. For Nova, the last save is the last checkpoint.
RTO is how long until things run again. For Nova, that is the time to claim a warm VM and freshen it.
Notice that a smaller RPO means saving more often, which is why we checkpoint after every good step.
clips.after: Nova's RPO is at most one step of work, and its RTO is about a minute, because the warm pool has a machine ready.

clips.title: Durable Agents: How to Build AI Systems That Survive a Crash with Samuel Colvin
clips.why: A live crash: an agent's worker is killed mid-run, and the run continues from where it was instead of starting over.
look: The completed activities are not run again after the crash; their results come from the history.
Retries happen by themselves, with no code in the agent for it.
Compare with our case: Temporal protects the workflow, and checkpoints protect the work that happened on the VM.
clips.after: Temporal keeps ticketToPr alive through a crash of the orchestrator; the checkpoint commits do the same job for the work inside the VM, which Temporal cannot see.

clips.title: EC2 Spot Instances Explained: Save Up to 90% on AWS Compute Costs
clips.why: Spot machines can be taken back by AWS with a short warning, and only work that can be interrupted belongs on them.
look: The interruption warning comes two minutes before the machine is taken.
The good use cases are jobs that can stop and continue.
Ask yourself what makes a CI fix interruptible and a person's question not.
clips.after: Routines like the CI fixer run on Spot because a checkpoint plus recovery makes an interruption cheap; Nova stays on normal machines because it waits for people.

practice.q: Complete the checkpoint commit message for step "add the empty-state card".
practice.hint: A marker GitHub Actions understands, in square brackets.
practice.why: Backend CI runs on a push to any branch; the marker keeps every checkpoint from starting it. The commit that opens the PR has no marker.

practice.q: Put the recovery from a frozen VM in order.
items: The harness pushes a checkpoint after step 3 and the heartbeat carries its sha
After 5 minutes with no heartbeat, workInSandbox throws SandboxDead
runWithRecovery claims a fresh VM and freshens it at the step 3 commit
The harness resumes the stored session and starts step 4 again
practice.why: Saving comes before failing: recovery can only start from what already left the machine.

practice.q: workInSandbox throws an error of type ScopeDenied (the broker refused something). What does runWithRecovery do?

options.text: Counts a lost VM and claims a fresh one
options.why: Only SandboxDead and LabNotReady mean a lost VM. A fresh VM would be refused the same way.

options.text: Rethrows it, so the caller sees a real failure
options.why: Recovery is for machines that died, not for errors in what the run is allowed to do.

options.text: Ignores it and returns the last checkpoint
options.why: Hiding a failure would report success for work that did not happen.

practice.q: Why does the heartbeat come from a timer in nova-worker and not from the model loop?

options.text: A long thinking turn would look like a dead VM if only the model sent heartbeats
options.why: The timer runs beside the claude process, so slow thinking is never taken for death.

options.text: The model is not allowed to call the broker
options.why: The model does reach the broker through our tools. The reason is timing, not permission.

options.text: Timers are cheaper than model calls
options.why: True, but beside the point: the heartbeat must keep its rhythm whatever the model is doing.

practice.q: After how many lost VMs on one ticket does the run stop and call a person?
practice.why: The first loss is replaced; the second is a pattern, so the run ends as needing a person, with the branch and notes kept.
